# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge cases described in the forum digest.

# Bank Statement Labeling Codebase Report

## Directory structure overview

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # Flask/gunicorn service on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Package: Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, sklearn, scipy
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + bank routing + pipeline orchestration
        ├── BankScripts/                # Per-bank narration parsers (35 banks)
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...
        │   └── (each: categorize_<Bank>_transactions)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Cross-bank enrichment
            ├── AppUtil.py              # Input cleaning + field splitters (/, -, :, etc.)
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Shared subcategory/merchant regexes
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Bank-specific extract patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # Subcategory + merchantType from name/narration
            ├── CleanName.py            # Brand/merchant name normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── CardCleanNames.py / CardPurpose.py  # Credit-card path
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Heuristic salary clustering
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer fuzzy match
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM L1/L2 categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # Human-readable summary
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── TransactionCategoryEnums.py / TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**No test suite** exists under `/app` (no `tests/`, `*_test.py`, or specs).  
**Git history**: single commit `0a1b6a3 import codebase` (2026-07-15). No multi-commit regression trail.  
**File mtimes**: most files `2022-11-02`; `HDFC.py` and `ICICI.py` touched `2026-07-15` (likely the hottest paths for the reported bugs).

---

## How the labeling pipeline works

### API entry

`POST /categorizeTransaction` in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`:

| Field | Role |
|--------|------|
| `bank` | Routes to bank script |
| `acc_type` | `SAVING` / `CURRENT` / `CREDIT_CARD` / … |
| `accountUID`, `accountHolder` | Logging + internal-payment match |
| `isPFMEnabled` | Optional PFM layer |
| `transactions[]` | Rows with `description`, `amount`, `type`, `remark`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate`, … |

### Per-bank pipeline (same shape for all banks)

```
clean_input_df
  → categorize_<BANK>_transactions(transactions, accountType)   # L1 category + partyName + some L2
  → [CREDIT_CARD only] card_clean_names → card_purpose
  → purpose(transactions, accountType)                          # cross-bank L2 + merchantType + some L1 overrides
  → clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)                # brand canonicalization of partyName
  → [if accountHolder] internal_payment(...)                    # INTERNAL_PAYMENT sub-tag
  → [if SAVING] salary_detection(...)                           # heuristic SALARY / REIMBURSEMENT
  → [if isPFMEnabled] pfm_categorization → simple_description
```

### What each stage produces

1. **Bank script** (`BankScripts/*.py`)  
   - Ordered `np.select` rule lists (first match wins within a block).  
   - Sets:
     - `transactionCategory` (L1): NEFT, UPI, CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, TRANSFER, REVERSAL, AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE, …
     - `transactionSubcategory` (partial L2): SALARY, LOAN, etc. when bank-specific
     - `partyName` / `party2` via slash/dash/colon splits and regex extract
     - sometimes `merchantType`
   - **Default L1** when nothing matches: `"TRANSFER"`.

2. **`purpose()`** (`UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`)  
   - Regex over `description` / `partyName` / `party2` → L2 (SALARY, LOAN_REPAYMENT, UTILITY_BILL, FOOD_RESTAURANT, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, …).  
   - Merchant-type tags (NBFC, Electricity, Flight, …).  
   - Clears L2 for bounce/charges/reversal-like L1s.  
   - Does **not** re-extract payees.

3. **`clean_names()`** (`UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`)  
   - Maps noisy `partyName` → canonical brands (“Swiggy”, “DMart”, …).  
   - Not the primary payee extractor.

4. **`salary_detection()`**  
   - Clusters by Levenshtein on `party2`; needs non-empty `partyName`, amount > 2999, excludes UPI/IMPS/reversals/deposits, etc.  
   - Can promote credits to `SALARY` / demote small ones to `REIMBURSEMENT`.

5. **`internal_payment()`**  
   - Fuzzy-matches `partyName` to `accountHolder` for transfer-like L1s.

### How “rules” work

Rules are **not** a config DSL. They are **hard-coded ordered condition lists**:

```python
conditions_choices = [
  [boolean_series, "LABEL_OR_EXTRACTED_SERIES"],
  ...
]
transactions['field'] = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default=...)
```

Shared helpers in `AppUtil.py`:

- `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` → join slash segments `[n1:n2]`
- `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_star`, …
- `py_extract(description, pat, index)` → regex capture group

Shared pattern libraries:

- `RegexConstants.py` — purpose keywords (SALARY, LOAN, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, …)
- `BankRegexConstants.py` — bank FT/CHQ/POS/NEFT extract patterns

---

## Key files (absolute paths + role)

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | Routes banks; wires full pipeline |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` | HDFC L1 + party extract; cheque-by-remark; bare-6-digit salary; debit→credit bounce/reversal |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` | ICICI L1 + heavy `/`-field party extract (BIL/, INF/, MMT/); bounce/reversal shift rules |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/SBI.py` | SBI; `TRANSFER TO` / `TRANSFER FROM` party logic |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py` | Axis; slash transfers; `Trf From` cleanup |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | Other banks: same pattern |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Cross-bank L2 + merchantType |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Payee brand cleanup |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | SALARY / bounce / merchant regexes |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | HDFC_FT_*, HDFC_CHQ_*, FT_PATTERN*, BANK_VER_*, etc. |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Post-hoc salary heuristics |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | Splitters + fuzzy_match |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Self-transfer tagging |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | PFM buckets (maps bounce/reversal → REVERSAL) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | L1 enum labels |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | L2 enum labels |

**Tests:** none in repo.

**Recent changes:** only one git commit; `HDFC.py` / `ICICI.py` are the only bank scripts with newer mtimes — prioritize those for regressions.

---

## Bug-by-bug: where it likely lives

### Bug 1 — Long all-numeric credit no longer cheque deposit; bare numeric salary loses SALARY

**Primary: bank L1 rules + HDFC salary subtype + accountType mismatch + salary_detection filters**

#### Cheque deposit via long numeric reference

Many banks treat **short numeric remarks** as cheque:

- HDFC (`HDFC.py` ~100):  
  `remark` length **exactly 15** and `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`
- Axis / BOM / Kotak / PNB / YES / UCO / RBL / KarurVyasa: remark `^[0-9]{3,6}$` (or similar) → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`

If the product now sees **longer** all-numeric refs (or non-zero-padded 15-char refs), the HDFC rule fails and L1 falls through to default **`TRANSFER`**.

Also relevant: description-based CHQ/CLG rules only fire when narration still contains CHQ/Cheque/CLG. Pure numeric description/remark with no CHQ token → TRANSFER.

#### Bare numeric salary code

HDFC bank-level salary (`HDFC.py` ~124):

```python
transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER")
  & description matches ^[0-9]{6}$
  & type CREDIT
  & accountType=="SAVINGS"   # <-- BUG: Controller/purpose use "SAVING"
  → SALARY
```

Everywhere else (Controller, Purpose, InternalPayment, ICICI) uses **`SAVING`**. This HDFC rule **never fires** if `acc_type` is `"SAVING"`.

Even if L1 is TRANSFER:

- `Purpose.py` SALARY regex (`RegexConstants.SALARY`) needs words like `salary`/`sal`/`payroll` — **not** bare digits.
- `SalaryDetection.py` requires `partyName` length > 0. HDFC blanks pure-numeric party names (`partyName` with no `[A-Za-z]` → `""` at ~261). So heuristic salary **cannot** attach either.

**Likely fix loci:**

1. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` lines ~100, ~124, ~261  
2. Similar remark→cheque rules in Axis/PNB/Kotak/YES/… if multi-bank  
3. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` / `SalaryDetection.py` if bare codes should promote without party name  
4. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` if FT vs CHQ patterns interact with numeric narrations  

---

### Bug 2 — Narration opens with direction word; counterparty empty/wrong

**Primary: bank `partyName` extract + cleanup of TO/FROM/TRF prefixes**

Direction handling is **bank-local**, incomplete, and inconsistent:

| Location | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `HDFC.py` ~253–257 | Strips `^By `, extracts after `Trf To` / `Paid To` / `Fund Trf To`; `^Trf ` → rest. No robust `From` / leading `To ` on raw description when category is TRANSFER |
| `HDFC.py` ~106 (`HDFC_CLEAN1` in BankRegexConstants) | Blanks names matching `transfer`, `Amt Trf To .*`, etc. |
| `ICICI.py` ~159 | `TRFR TO:|TRFR FROM:` → `py_extract(..., index=0)` — **index 0 is `TO`/`FROM`, not the name** (name is group 1) → wrong/empty counterparty |
| `ICICI.py` ~201–203, ~231–232 | IMPS-only ` To ` stripping; leading `To ` / `Trfto ` |
| `SBI.py` ~131–132 | `^TRANSFER TO ` / `^TRANSFER FROM ` with account-number strip |
| `Axis.py` ~167, ~181 | `TRANSFER TO `, `Trf From ` |
| `CityUnion.py`, `Indusind.py`, `StandardCharted.py`, `RBL.py` | Various TO/FROM extractors |
| `BankRegexConstants.TRF_STOP_WORDS` | Stop words for transfer narrations (SBI-oriented) |
| `CleanName.py` | Brand map only — does not fix direction prefixes |

**Likely failure modes:**

1. Party extract takes the whole narration; cleanup only covers a few prefixes → leftover “To …” or empty after over-strip.  
2. ICICI `TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)` with `index=0` is a clear wrong-group bug.  
3. HDFC TRANSFER extract (~200–201) takes first dash/slash field; if field 0 is `TO`/`FROM`/direction, name is wrong; later `[A-Za-z]` filter may blank it.  
4. Final filters blank names that look like pure direction tokens (`^Tr$`, transfer stop words).

**Likely fix loci:** bank partyName blocks (esp. **HDFC.py**, **ICICI.py**, **SBI.py**, **Axis.py**) + `BankRegexConstants.py` (`TRF_STOP_WORDS`, `FT_PATTERN*`, `HDFC_CLEAN1`).

---

### Bug 3 — Bill transfer `type/sub-type/numeric-ref/payee` pulls numeric ref as name

**Primary: ICICI (and similar) slash-segment indexing for BIL/ bill payments**

ICICI is the clearest match (`ICICI.py` ~147–151, refine ~193–206, blank ~233):

```text
^BIL/INFT/           count("/")==3  → sep_by_(..., 2, 3)
^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS|...  → sep_by_(..., 4, 5)
^BIL/BPAY|^BIL/RCHG  → sep_by_(..., 3, 4)
^BIL/00[12]...NSP0   → sep_by_(..., 4, 5)
^BIL/00[12]...(!NSP) → sep_by_(..., 2, 3)  # also strips digits
```

For a 4-field shape `type/sub-type/numericRef/payeeName`:

- Wrong index → **numeric ref becomes `partyName`**.  
- Later refine: if party is all digits `^[0-9]+$`, sometimes re-pick another segment (`INF/INFT/` ~206).  
- Final scrub (~233): `partyName` matching `[0-9]{6,}` → **`""`** (except CMS / INTERNAL_FUND_TRANSFER) — so you get either a number as name or empty, never the final payee.

Same class of bugs elsewhere:

- Axis TRANSFER with `count("/")` 1–2 → `sep_by_(..., 0, 1)` (first segment, not last)  
- HDFC TRANSFER one-slash → `sep_by_(..., 1, 2)` (second segment only)  
- Many NEFT/IMPS/BIL paths use fixed segment indices that break when banks add/remove middle ref fields  

**Likely fix loci:**

1. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` BIL/INF/MMT party extraction (~147–167, refine ~191–233)  
2. Analogous fixed-index slash parsers in Axis/BOB/HDFC  
3. Prefer “last non-numeric alpha segment” rather than hard-coded index for bill-style narrations  

---

### Bug 4 — Offsetting credit after matching debit labeled bounce, not reversal

**Primary: adjacent-row shift rules in bank L1 categorization**

Pattern appears in **HDFC** and **ICICI** (and similar spirit elsewhere):

**HDFC.py ~98–99:**

```python
# CREDIT, prev was DEBIT, same amount,
# description == description.shift(2),  # <-- periods=2
# and desc matches IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS  → REVERSAL

# CREDIT, prev DEBIT, same amount,
# description == description.shift(1)  → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

**ICICI.py ~49–50:**

```python
# same amount + same description as prev DEBIT + IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS → REVERSAL
# else same amount + same description as prev DEBIT → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

**Failure modes matching the bug report:**

1. **Order of rules / over-broad bounce:** Any matched debit→credit pair with identical narration becomes `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` unless the IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS branch wins. Offsetting **FT / ACH / generic TRANSFER / bill** credits get **bounce**, not **reversal**.  
2. **HDFC REVERSAL branch uses `shift(periods=2)`** for description equality while amount uses `shift(1)`. For a simple debit-then-credit pair, description often **doesn’t** equal two rows back → REVERSAL never matches → falls to bounce (or never matches if descriptions differ slightly). That looks like a regression bug.  
3. **Earlier explicit bounce rules** (HDFC ~27: SI/ACH/EMI patterns on CREDIT) can label bounce before the offsetting logic runs (`np.select` first-true wins).  
4. **Purpose.py ~173** clears subcategory for categories containing `BOUNCE`, so L2 doesn’t correct the mislabel.  
5. **PFMCategorization.py ~73** maps both REVERSAL and BOUNCE category strings into PFM `REVERSAL`, which can hide L1 mistakes in PFM-only views—but raw `transactionCategory` still shows bounce.

**Likely fix loci:**

1. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` lines 27, **98–99** (especially `shift(2)` vs `shift(1)`)  
2. `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` lines 18, **49–50**  
3. Same pattern if present in other banks (grep `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` + `shift(periods`)  
4. Optionally Purpose/PFM only if product expects L2 correction  

---

## Mental model of labels

| Output field | Set mainly by |
|--------------|----------------|
| `transactionCategory` (L1) | Bank script; small overrides in Purpose |
| `transactionSubcategory` (L2 / “sub-tag”) | Bank script (partial) → Purpose → InternalPayment → SalaryDetection |
| `partyName` / counterparty / payee | Bank script extract + refine; then CleanName brand map |
| `party2` | Compact lowercased partyName for matching |
| `merchantType` | Bank script + Purpose merchant rules |
| `isInternalPayment` | InternalPayment |
| `pfmCategoryOne/Two`, simple description | Optional PFM path |

---

## Suggested investigation order for the 4 bugs

1. Reproduce with `POST /categorizeTransaction` against HDFC + ICICI sample rows (numeric remark, bare 6-digit credit, `To/From …` narration, `BIL/…/12345/Payee`, debit+matching credit).  
2. **Bug 1:** Trace HDFC remark rule + `SAVINGS` vs `SAVING` + numeric party blanking.  
3. **Bug 2:** Trace party extract then direction cleanup; fix ICICI `TRFR` capture index.  
4. **Bug 3:** Print slash segments for failing BIL narrations; adjust indices or pick last alpha field.  
5. **Bug 4:** Fix HDFC `shift(2)` and narrow when identical debit/credit is bounce vs reversal (channel keywords, auto-pay categories only, etc.).  

I can next draft concrete failing fixtures and patch candidates for any one of these four if you want that.

Let me look more carefully at the bugs. The maintainer said these are edge form bugs. Let me try to reproduce them by writing a quick test script.
The bug is exactly where you spotted it: the regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` is 16 characters long, but HDFC statements are using 15-character remarks for those cheque deposits. That mismatch means the pattern never matched, so the row fell through to the generic-transfer rule instead of CHEQUE_DEPOSIT.

Salary sub-tag is also brittle—bare numeric codes are being caught by the generic rule rather than the salary rule, and the account-type check is looking for `"SAVINGS"` while HDFC returns `"SAVING"`.

For the direction-word issue, the ICICI pattern `TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)` is correct in spirit, but the HDFC side is fragile: `^Trf ` followed by `py_extract(..., "Trf (.*)")` will return `"From John"` instead of `"John"` when the narration is `"Trf From John"`.

steps.message:
Fixed four edge-case labeling bugs in HDFC and ICICI:

1. **Cheque / salary (HDFC)** — Remark cheque pattern was `11` zeros + 5 digits on a length-15 field (impossible); now `10` + 5. Salary sub-tag checked `SAVINGS` instead of `SAVING`.
2. **Direction-word payees** — ICICI `TRFR TO/FROM` used capture group 0 (direction); HDFC now extracts names after leading To/From/Trf prefixes.
3. **Bill slash fields (ICICI)** — Four-field `BIL/INFT/ref/payee` took the numeric ref (`2:3`); now takes the final payee (`3:4`), with a numeric-party fallback.
4. **Offsetting credit** — Matching debit→credit is `REVERSAL` (HDFC also had `shift(2)` → `shift(1)`); real ACH/SI/NACH bounces unchanged.
